title: LP2-54–55: the 8×8 word arrangement
question: Do the final two pages contain 64 non-heading words, and does that count specify a labyrinth route?
summary: Removing the one-rune-plus-eight red opening leaves exactly 64 words: 48 start on LP2-54 and 16 on LP2-55. The arrangement does not select a route.

scope.representation: Archived word-token export, independently reconstructed from both page transcriptions; first two opening tokens excluded.
scope.procedure: Count remaining words by page of start, arrange in manuscript order as eight columns, and enumerate eight simple inward-spiral variants.
scope.parameters: One 66-word source span; two opening tokens excluded; 64 remaining cells; eight fixed routes without scoring.
scope.exclusions: Other word-boundary transcriptions, visual maze walls, arbitrary traversals, rune transformations and plaintext.

finding: The 64-word arrangement reproduces after removing the two opening tokens. Its 48/16 page split gives a six-row/two-row boundary. The count leaves multiple routes and no output operation.
limitations: The heading exclusion follows the source proposal and visible red opening. A square count does not establish an intended labyrinth route or decipherment.
next_steps: Fix start, turning rule, readout and validation target before interpreting words; compare with other fixed routes on held-out text.

visuals.caption: Word positions 1–64 in an eight-column grid, distinguishing their page of start.
